meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots and dull skin in India**, the safest general pick is a **stable 10–15% vitamin C serum** with supportive ingredients like **niacinamide, vitamin E, ferulic acid, or hyaluronic acid**; this range is repeatedly recommended for most users, while higher strengths can work faster but may irritate sensitive skin.[2][17][8]

If you want a practical buying choice, here’s the simplest way to decide:

| Your skin / need | Better pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Beginner / sensitive skin** | **Pilgrim 10% Vitamin C Face Serum** | Recommended as a gentler daily option with vitamin C plus niacinamide and soothing ingredients.[2] |
| **Stubborn dark spots** | **Pilgrim 15% Vitamin C Face Serum** or **La Roche-Posay Pure 12%** | Higher strength is suggested for more persistent pigmentation; LRP is cited as a strong premium option.[2][1] |
| **Budget / strongest potency** | **The Ordinary Vitamin C 23%** | Cited as a high-potency value option for pigmentation, though it may be more irritating.[1] |
| **If you prefer a stable vitamin C form for Indian climate** | **Ethyl ascorbic acid-based serum** | Sources note ethyl ascorbic acid is more stable in heat/humidity and still brightens well.[3][17] |

If you want the **one most balanced recommendation**, I’d choose a **10%–15% serum with ethyl ascorbic acid or L-ascorbic acid plus niacinamide/vitamin E/ferulic acid** because it gives a good mix of **brightness, dark-spot fading, and tolerability** for Indian skin and climate.[2][3][17]

A few buying rules matter more than the brand name:
- **10%** is usually the sweet spot for first-time users and daily use.[2][17]
- **15–20%** is better if your dark spots are stubborn and your skin tolerates actives well.[17][10]
- Look for **sunscreen use every morning**, because vitamin C works best when paired with sun protection for pigmentation.[2][9]
- If your skin is sensitive, avoid jumping straight to very high concentrations.[17][8]

If you want, I can next give you:
- a **best vitamin C serum under ₹500 / ₹1000 / ₹2000 in India**, or
- a **shortlist by skin type**: oily, dry, sensitive, or acne-prone.
